name: Grand Prairie
seo_title: Grand Prairie, TX Christmas Events for Kids 2026: 10 Events
seo_description: Grand Prairie kids' Christmas: Main Street Magic parade and tree lighting, Prairie Lights, Paws on the Prairie, Traders Village and Santa brunch.
lede: The story of Christmas in Grand Prairie starts in 1863, when A. M. Dechman swapped a broken wagon for 239 acres, and in 1876, when the Texas and Pacific Railway arrived, and today it runs from the Main Street Magic parade and tree lighting downtown to Prairie Lights at Lynn Creek Park. Grand Prairie has 10 events on this page, led by Main Street Magic on Saturday, December 5, 2026.
sections: A broken wagon and a railroad depot

The Handbook of Texas says the community was organized in 1863, when A. M. Dechman's wagon broke down on a trip to Fort Belknap. He traded the wagon, his ox team and 200 dollars in Confederate money for a 239 acre tract. The post office opened in 1874 as Dechman or Deckman, and in 1876 the Texas and Pacific Railway was built to the site. Dechman gave the railroad alternating lots in exchange for a depot. In 1877 the post office took the name Grand Prairie to match the railroad, said to come from a woman stepping off a train and saying, what a grand prairie.
The Interurban, Hensley Field and a wartime boom

The North Texas Traction Company, better known as the Interurban, began service to Grand Prairie in the 1900s, and the town incorporated in 1902 with S. R. Lively as mayor. Dallas built Hensley Field nearby in 1928, and by 1941 the North American Aviation plant had 5,000 employees. At its peak it employed 38,500 workers, and between 1940 and the end of the war the population grew from 1,595 to 18,000. The plant shut down on August 14, 1945, yet the city recovered and reached 99,606 people in 1990. The Texas Almanac lists 196,100 for 2020.
Christmas downtown and across the city

Main Street Magic, the city's Christmas Tree Lighting and Parade, is Saturday, December 5, 2026, at 6 pm in Downtown Grand Prairie, and the city lists it as free. Winter Wonderland at Grand Prairie City Hall follows on December 17 from 6 to 8 pm, and Paws on the Prairie: Holiday Edition fills downtown on December 19 from 2 to 6 pm. Prairie Lights, a two mile drive through light display at Lynn Creek Park, runs November 26 through December 31, with car passes sold online. Traders Village also holds The Christmas Market on weekends from November 28 through December 20.
trains: Grand Prairie grew up on rails: the Texas and Pacific Railway reached it in 1876 and the Interurban began service in the 1900s. Trinity Railway Express lists CentrePort / DFW Airport Station in Fort Worth, and Medical/Market Center and EBJ Union Station in Dallas. DART's Blue Line runs from Downtown Rowlett to UNT Dallas Station. For a train outing, the Interurban Railway Museum is in Plano, the Museum of the American Railroad is in Frisco and the McKinney Avenue M-Line Trolley runs in Dallas.

faq: How did Grand Prairie get its name?

The post office first called the community Dechman or Deckman in 1874. In 1877 it adopted the name Grand Prairie to agree with the railroad, which had used that name since 1873. The Handbook of Texas says the name supposedly came from a woman who stepped off the train and said, what a grand prairie.

A. M. Dechman founded the community in 1863 after his wagon broke down on a trip from Jacksonville, Texas, to Fort Belknap. He traded the wagon, ox team and 200 dollars in Confederate money for a 239 acre tract, then platted the townsite and gave the railroad alternating lots in exchange for a depot.
What did the railroad and the Interurban mean for Grand Prairie?

The Texas and Pacific Railway was built to the site in 1876, which turned the settlement into a shipping point for cotton, grain and livestock. The North Texas Traction Company, known as the Interurban, began service in the 1900s, and the town incorporated in 1902 with S. R. Lively as mayor, says the Handbook of Texas.
Why did Grand Prairie grow so fast in the 1940s?

Dallas built Hensley Field nearby in 1928, and in 1941 the North American Aviation plant had 5,000 employees, rising to 38,500 at its peak. Between 1940 and the end of World War II Grand Prairie grew from 1,595 to 18,000 people, according to the Handbook of Texas, before the plant shut down on August 14, 1945.
What is Main Street Magic in Grand Prairie?

Main Street Magic is the City of Grand Prairie's Christmas Tree Lighting and Parade. In 2026 it is Saturday, December 5, at 6 pm in Downtown Grand Prairie, 300 W Main St, and the city lists it as free. Winter Wonderland at City Hall on December 17 is another free city holiday event.
Is there a Christmas lights display in Grand Prairie?

Yes. Prairie Lights is a drive through light display at Lynn Creek Park, 5610 Lake Ridge Parkway, open November 26 through December 31, 2026, from 6 pm. The City of Grand Prairie Parks, Arts and Recreation listing shows a $50 general admission car pass, with a $35 early bird price for visits November 30 to December 4.
